semantics.note: Faithful two-part observation. 'Essentially every' is softened to 'none' in the normalisation, but the scope is the broad warned-of harms either way.

contract.note: Plain reading of 'nothing' as no substantive technical disclosure is ordinary, and splitting the two components is reasonable. Result depends on treating generic architecture, objective, data source and RLHF disclosure as substantive.

evidence.note: March 2023 system card describes broad risks as needing further research and mitigations as reducing, not eliminating, harms. Supports the 'none are solved' part.
Technical report discloses Transformer architecture, next-token pretraining, data sources and RLHF fine-tuning, while withholding further detail. Contradicts the literal 'told nothing' part.

reviews.rationale: The unsolved-harms component holds: the launch materials present the risks as mitigated, not eliminated. The disclosure component fails on the plain reading, because OpenAI did publish basic but substantive facts about architecture, training objective, data and RLHF, though it withheld most details. So the claim is mixed: harms part supported, 'nothing' part contradicted.

reviews.rationale: OpenAI's own launch disclosure, an admission against interest, says the model still fabricates facts and needs verification. That meets the support condition. Reduced hallucination relative to GPT-3.5 does not meet the contradiction condition of reliable fabrication-free retrieval.
